examples: My score on this exam is really good.
The exam score comes out tomorrow.
nuance: 점수 is the number of points you get on a test or game, and Koreans say 점수가 나오다 when results are released. It is more specific than 성적, which covers your overall grades.
mistakes: Confusing 점수 the score with 성적 the grades

examples: The answer is in the textbook.
I study with a Korean textbook.
nuance: 교과서 is the official book for a school subject that students learn from in class. A blank book for writing is a 공책, so the two words are not the same thing.
mistakes: Confusing 교과서 the textbook with 공책 the notebook

examples: The pencil is in the pencil case.
My pencil case is on the desk.
I bought a new pencil case.
nuance: 필통 holds your pens and pencils, and the word joins 필 for writing tools with 통 for a case. Students keep a 연필 and 지우개 inside it during class.
mistakes: Confusing 필통 the case with 연필 the pencil itself

examples: The textbook is in the school bag.
I carry my school bag every day.
My school bag is very heavy.
nuance: 책가방 is the bag students carry their books in, joining 책 for book with 가방 for bag. Koreans use the verb 메다 for wearing it on the back, unlike holding a handbag.
mistakes: Using 들다 instead of 메다 for a backpack

examples: The students play soccer at the playground.
Our school playground is really wide.
nuance: 운동장 is the open field at a school where students exercise and play sports. Use 에서 for what you do there and 에 when you go to it.
mistakes: Using 에 instead of 에서 for playing there

examples: I meet my friend at the school gate.
We wait in front of the gate.
I pass the school gate in the morning.
nuance: 교문 is the main gate at the entrance of a school, joining 교 for school with 문 for door. Students often meet friends 교문 앞에서, in front of the gate, before class.
mistakes: Confusing 교문 the school gate with 문 any door

examples: Our school uniform is very pretty.
저는 매일 교복을 입고 학교에 가요.
I wear my uniform to school every day.
nuance: 교복 is the required uniform students wear at school, joining 교 for school with 복 for clothes. Koreans use the verb 입다 to wear it, the same verb for any clothing.
mistakes: Using 신다 instead of 입다 for a uniform

examples: The students eat the school meal at lunch.
Today the school meal is really tasty.
I talk with my friend at meal time.
nuance: 급식 is the meal provided at a school or workplace, usually eaten together at lunch. A meal you buy yourself at a restaurant is just 밥 or 식사, not 급식.
mistakes: Using 급식 for a meal you cook at home

examples: I pay the tuition every month.
This academy tuition is a bit expensive.
The tuition went up a little this year.
nuance: 수업료 is the money you pay to take classes, joining 수업 for lesson with 료 for fee. Koreans say 수업료를 내다 to pay it, using the verb 내다 for fees.
mistakes: Using 사다 instead of 내다 for paying a fee

examples: I received a scholarship this term.
If your grades are good a scholarship comes.
My sister applied for a scholarship.
nuance: 장학금 is money given to a student for good grades or need, so they can keep studying. Koreans say 장학금을 받다 to get one, the natural verb for receiving money.
mistakes: Using 돈 the general money for a 장학금

examples: We practice together in the club.
My friend is a member of a photo club.
nuance: 동아리 is a student club where people who share a hobby meet and do it together. To join one Koreans say 동아리에 들어가다, using the verb for entering a group.
mistakes: Using 모임 a casual gathering for a school 동아리

examples: I live in the school dormitory.
We study together in the dormitory.
The dormitory is inside the school.
nuance: 기숙사 is a building where students or workers live together near a school or job. To say you live there Koreans use 살다 with the location particle, as in 기숙사에 살다.
mistakes: Confusing 기숙사 the dormitory with 집 a private home
